medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends aspirin 75‑81 mg OD for all IHD patients (first‑line antiplatelet).

medications.duration: 12 months from acute STEMI (if still within period)
medications.purpose: Dual antiplatelet therapy after recent ACS
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG185 advises aspirin + ticagrelor or prasugrel for 12 months after ACS.

medications.purpose: Cardioprotective ACE‑I for IHD, hypertension and diabetic nephropathy
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends an ACE‑I for all IHD patients, especially with hypertension, diabetes or LV dysfunction.

medications.purpose: High‑intensity lipid‑lowering to achieve >40 % non‑HDL‑C reduction
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 advises atorvastatin 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20‑40 mg for all IHD patients (high‑intensity statin).

medications.purpose: Blood pressure control and volume management
medications.nice_justification: Hypertension management is part of NICE IHD care; thiazide is first‑line antihypertensive.

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily (titrate to HR 55‑60 bpm, max 10 mg)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 lists cardio‑selective beta‑blockers (e.g., bisoprolol) as first‑line anti‑anginal therapy.

medications.dose: 0.4 mg up to 3 doses within 15 min for acute chest pain (PRN)
medications.nice_justification: NICE acute management recommends sublingual GTN for acute angina attacks.

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and thiazide can raise serum potassium and affect renal function.
interactions_checked.action: Check eGFR and serum K⁺ at baseline, 2 weeks after dose increase, then every 3 months; consider reducing thiazide dose if K⁺ >5.5 mmol/L.

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential increased risk of myopathy, especially with renal impairment.
interactions_checked.action: Obtain baseline CK and liver enzymes; repeat CK at 3 months and if muscle symptoms develop.

interactions_checked.interaction: Beta‑blocker may blunt reflex tachycardia from GTN but combination is safe.
interactions_checked.action: Educate patient on nitrate‑free interval (≥8 h) and monitor for hypotension.

interactions_checked.interaction: Dual antiplatelet therapy; increased bleeding risk but indicated post‑ACS.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; continue for 12 months as per guideline.

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure not recorded – assume target <130/80 mmHg (diabetic) and will be measured at each visit.
Liver function tests (ALT/AST) and CK not provided – required before initiating high‑intensity atorvastatin; will order baseline labs.

Serum potassium is 5.2 mmol/L (mildly high) – ACE‑I uptitration may worsen hyperkalaemia; monitoring plan included.

treatment_summary: The plan aligns with NICE CG126/NG185 for secondary prevention of ischemic heart disease: continue lifelong aspirin, maintain prasugrel for 12 months post‑STEMI, up‑titrate lisinopril to 10 mg, switch to high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg, replace propranolol with cardio‑selective bisoprolol 5 mg (titrated), continue hydrochlorothiazide, and add sublingual GTN PRN for breakthrough angina. Monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, CK, liver enzymes, blood pressure and heart rate is incorporated, and lifestyle advice (smoking cessation, Mediterranean diet, exercise, weight management) should be reinforced.
